evidence: src/presentation/http/LoanController.ts LoanController.lend: `const loan = await this.lending.lend(...); await this.history.note(loan.id, 'lent');` makes the controller decide that each loan must be recorded in history, which is a domain workflow rule.

src/presentation/http/LoanController.ts LoanController.giveBack: `const fine = await this.lending.giveBack(body.loanId, new Date()); await this.history.note(body.loanId, 'returned');` does the same for returns, so the controller coordinates two business services.
Presentation work that is correctly placed: LendRequest/ReturnRequest DTOs, HttpResult status codes 201/200, renderLoan(loan) view mapping, and historyOf, which only delegates.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of LoanController is ordinary presentation work. It defines the request DTOs (LendRequest, ReturnRequest), maps status codes into HttpResult and renders the loan through renderLoan. But the controller also decides the business workflow. After each lending operation it records a history event itself: 'lent' after lend and 'returned' after giveBack. The rule that every lend and every return must be written to the loan history is a domain rule, and it belongs in the business layer (LendingService or a business-layer use case). With the rule in the controller, any other entry point that calls LendingService would skip the history record. This call is borderline: some reviewers would accept a thin controller that calls two services. So confidence is moderate.

violations.message: LoanController.lend and LoanController.giveBack contain the business workflow rule that every lend and return must be recorded in the loan history (history.note(..., 'lent'/'returned') after the LendingService call). This domain responsibility belongs in the business layer, e.g. inside LendingService or a business use case, not in the presentation controller.
